Leanness
lēn´nĕs
n. (wasting; want of flesh; a soul made thin; Hebrew razon, razeh)
From lean, Old English hlæne, thin, wanting flesh. Scripture uses it for the body wasting and, more terribly, for the soul.

Biblical Definition

Leanness is emptiness that shows. Job sees it as an accuser: “And thou hast filled me with wrinkles, which is a witness against me: and my leanness rising up in me beareth witness to my face” (Job 16:8). But the gravest use in Scripture is not of the body at all. Of Israel in the wilderness, demanding flesh to eat, the psalmist writes: “And he gave them their request; but sent leanness into their soul” (Psa 106:15). That is the whole doctrine of answered prayer in half a verse. God can grant a request as a judgment. Isaiah applies the word to Assyria's glory: “Therefore shall the Lord, the Lord of hosts, send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory he shall kindle a burning like the burning of a fire” (Isa 10:16). And the prophet takes it on himself in a cry that stands almost alone in the canon for sheer weight: “But I said, My leanness, my leanness, woe unto me!” (Isa 24:16). Fatness in Scripture is not gluttony but abundance and blessing; leanness is its withdrawal. The soul can starve at a full table.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines leanness as destitution of fat; want of flesh; thinness of body; and figuratively, want of matter, poverty, emptiness.

expand to see more

LEANNESS, n. Destitution of fat; want of flesh; thinness of body; meagerness.

2. Want of matter; poverty; emptiness; as the leanness of a purse.

LEAN, a. Wanting flesh; meager; not fat; thin.

Key Scripture

Job 16:8 — "And thou hast filled me with wrinkles, which is a witness against me: and my leanness rising up in me beareth witness to my face."

Psa 106:15 — "And he gave them their request; but sent leanness into their soul."

Isa 10:16 — "Therefore shall the Lord, the Lord of hosts, send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory he shall kindle a burning like the burning of a fire."

Isa 24:16 — "From the uttermost part of the earth have we heard songs, even glory to the righteous. But I said, My leanness, my leanness, woe unto me! the treacherous dealers have dealt treacherously; yea, the treacherous dealers have dealt very treacherously."

Modern Corruption

Answered prayer is treated as proof of God's favour, when Psalm 106 records a request granted and leanness sent with it.

expand to see more

Psalm 106:15 is one of the most neglected verses in Scripture and one of the most necessary. Israel wanted flesh; the LORD gave them flesh; and the same sentence reports that He sent leanness into their soul. The prosperity teaching that reads every granted request as divine approval has no place to put this verse. Neither does the softer popular version of it, which assumes that if a door opened the LORD must have wanted us through it. Sometimes the door opens because we would not stop knocking.

The corrective is not to distrust God's generosity but to distrust our appetite. Israel's petition was not for anything wicked in itself — it was for meat. What condemned it was that it despised the manna already given. A soul can be made thin by getting exactly what it asked for, and the wilderness generation is Scripture's standing exhibit.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew razon (H7332), leanness, wasting; razeh (H7330), lean; the opposite of dashen, fatness, which in Scripture means abundance and blessing.

expand to see more

Hebrew razon (H7332) — leanness, wasting; Psalm 106:15, Isaiah 10:16.

Hebrew kachash (H3585) — leanness, failing; Job 16:8.

Hebrew razi (H7334) — my leanness; Isaiah 24:16, the prophet's cry.

Hebrew nephesh (H5315) — soul; what the leanness of Psalm 106 was sent into.

Hebrew dashen (H1878) — to be fat, to be made rich; the blessing leanness reverses.

Usage

"“He gave them their request; but sent leanness into their soul” — a granted prayer as judgment."

"“My leanness, my leanness, woe unto me” — Isaiah's cry in the midst of songs."

"“Therefore shall the Lord, the Lord of hosts, send among his fat ones leanness” — glory withdrawn from Assyria."
